items_missed: No agenda statement — said 'I just need to gather a few details about this move in order for me to be able to book you' but never gave the 10-15 minute timeframe and never asked 'sound good?'

Never recapped the quote already discussed. Kelsey opened with 'I spoke with you yesterday about getting pricing' and Arden rebuilt the entire quote from scratch, re-asking name, phone, email, addresses and square footage.
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops on either end of the move.

Never asked the moving-stressor question ('is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?'). He twice asked the generic 'do you have any question, any clarification regarding the moving process in general?' — that is not the same question and it surfaced nothing.
No zip codes captured for either address — origin and destination were taken by street address only.
No day-of-week rate tier offered. Quoted a flat $200/hr for a Saturday 9/19 move without telling her whether a weekday would be cheaper.

Save Your Ass prep speech entirely absent — no 'prep before move day = shorter move = lower bill', no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, no sense-check close. This was the highest-value miss on the call: a 16th-floor condo with a 100-foot hallway walk is exactly the job where consolidation cuts real hours off the bill.
Traffic never mentioned as a variable despite a 35-40 minute Tampa-to-Largo leg on a Saturday.
Never asked whether any furniture needs disassembly/reassembly (a 1BR with a bed frame almost certainly does) so that time is not in the 4-5 hour estimate.

Booking close failed. Kelsey opened the call saying 'I would like to go ahead and book with your company' and the call ended with her asking to step away to make a phone call. Arden said 'no problem ma'am, I'll send you an email' — no attempt to hold the 9/19 date, no callback time set, no 'let me pencil you in, you can change it any time since there's no deposit.'
Never said 'any other questions before I let you go?' at the close.
Never gave hours of operation or how to reach the team back.
Never explained the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or asked her to reply with corrections.
Used the customer's name only once (the opening 'good morning Kelsey'); everything after that was 'ma'am' — needs 3+ name uses.
Insurance explanation covered the $2,000 No Worries coverage and zero deductible but never gave the 60 cents/lb baseline for contrast.

Clarity and pace issues throughout: 'September ninety', 'it's a one bunch of condo', 'boxes typically for 82', 'Jake path'. Kelsey had to say 'say that one more time' twice, and he repeated one full question verbatim word-for-word.
Dead air while working the system ('give me one second... bear with me, I'm still here') with no bridge to fill it.
top_strength: The probe and the estimate build were genuinely excellent — the best part of this call by a distance. Arden systematically worked origin and destination: 16th floor, freight elevator reservation, parking off Polk Street, then actively coached her through measuring the hallway walk using the school bus reference ('let's use a school bus as a reference') and landed on 100 feet. He ran the full specialty-item sweep in order — heavy/oversized, fragile/valuable, appliances, TV, boxes — and handled the glass coffee table on the spot with 'we can wrap that in moving blankets.' He then tied every one of those details back into the estimate out loud: 'since we're moving you from the sixteenth floor with elevator access and a bit of a walk from your apartment down to the parking into a two story town home which is around 35 to forty minutes away... I'm estimating the move to take approximately around four to five hours.' His clock explanation was flawless (on-site start, contract opens, 2.5 hour minimum, 15-minute increments, 'does that all make sense?') and his handling of the $105 transportation fee pushback was calm and specific — he named the exact address and the 35-40 minute distance rather than getting defensive.
coaching_note: LIVE OPERATIONAL RISK, fix before 9/19: Kelsey said 'I have reserved the elevator for the nineteenth and the earliest that I could do would be 10:00 AM.' Arden replied that the team arrives 8:30-9:00 and 'that should be fine.' It is not fine — the clock starts on site when the contract opens, so as quoted she gets billed for up to 90 minutes of movers standing in the lobby waiting for a freight elevator she cannot release until 10. Either move the crew arrival to 9:45 or get the note into EMMA that the clock does not open until elevator access. This needs to be corrected in the file and in her confirmation email. Second, the highest-leverage sales fix: this was a customer who opened the call saying she wanted to book, and she hung up unbooked. The moment she said 'can you keep my information in your system while I make a phone call,' the line should have been 'Absolutely — and since there's no deposit and nothing to pay today, let me go ahead and hold September 19th under your name right now so nobody else takes it. If your call changes anything, one phone call from you and it's off, no charge. What time works for me to check back with you today?' A hold costs nothing and converts a warm caller. Third, run the Save Your Ass speech — on a 16th-floor unit with a 100-foot hallway it is worth real money to her: 'Kelsey, the single biggest thing that lowers your bill is prep. Anything that fits in your car — the patio chairs, loose drawer items, the pictures off the walls, the kids' stuff — take a carload over yourself. Boxes stacked by the door instead of spread across rooms saves us trips down that hallway. Every 15 minutes you save us is money off your final bill. Does that make sense?' Fourth, stop rebuilding quotes from zero — she told you she spoke with you yesterday, so open with 'I've got your details right here from yesterday, let me just confirm a couple of things' instead of re-asking her name, phone, email and square footage. It reads as disorganized to a customer who already gave you all of it. Last, verify the rate: a flat $200/hr was quoted for a Saturday with no weekday alternative offered — confirm that matches Tampa's Sat tier in EMMA, and if a weekday is cheaper she deserved to hear it.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite and patient ('ma'am' throughout, 'thank you so much', 'no problem'), but transactional and script-driven with no rapport moments, only one use of her name, and he apologized rather than reframed value when she pushed back on the $105 fee ('sorry for that ma'am').
audio_review_reason: Clarity signal worth verifying on audio: Kelsey asked 'say that one more time' twice, Arden repeated an entire question verbatim, and the transcript is heavily garbled with self-corrections ('September ninety', 'one bunch of condo', 'boxes typically for 82'). Need to hear whether this is transcription noise or a real intelligibility problem for the customer.
